title: A practical randomized trust-region method to escape saddle points in high dimension
summary: Without randomization, escaping the saddle points of $f \colon \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$ requires at least $Ω(d)$ pieces of information about $f$ (values, gradients, Hessian-vector products). With randomization, this can be reduced to a polylogarithmic dependence in $d$. The prototypical algorithm to that effect is perturbed gradient descent (PGD): through sustained jitter, it reliably escapes strict saddle points. However, it also never settles: there is no convergence. What is more, PGD requires precise tuning based on Lipschitz constants and a preset target accuracy. To improve on…
